terms.gloss: keen-scented, with a sharp nose; quick to perceive
evidence: Plaut. Curc. 1.2.17: sagāx nāsum habet (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Chiefly of dogs’ sense of smell; hence of the mind, sagacious. Traupman gives the superlative sagācissimus.

sources: Lewis & Short: sagax
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 336.
